remember: Child adoption leave: up to 180 days for adoptive mothers (Rule 102A).
Paternity leave: up to 10 days, for two deliveries, before or within three months after delivery (Rule 102B).
Hospital leave is not debited to the leave account and can be combined with other leave (Rule 106).

questions.q: For how many days can child adoption leave be granted?
questions.why: Rule 102A allows up to 180 days to female employees who are adoptive mothers.

questions.q: Paternity leave of up to 10 days is allowed for how many deliveries?
questions.why: KSR Part I Rule 102B grants it for two deliveries.

questions.q: Paternity leave may be taken up to 10 days before, or within how long after, the date of delivery?
questions.why: KSR Part I Rule 102B(a): before or within three months after delivery.

questions.q: Hospital leave salary for the first 120 days is equal to which leave salary?
questions.why: KSR Part I Rule 104: earned leave salary for 120 days, then half pay leave salary.

questions.q: Hospital leave is treated how with respect to the leave account?
options: Not debited to the leave account
questions.why: KSR Part I Rule 106: not debited and may be combined with other admissible leave.

remember: Retrospective commutation is into any kind of leave admissible when the original leave was granted (Rule 76).
No commutation after one year from the date of sanction of leave (Rule 76 / 89(i)).
Officer cannot claim retrospective commutation as a right; arrears are drawn or overdrawn amounts recovered (Rule 89).

questions.q: What is the time limit for retrospective commutation of leave?
options: One year from the date of sanction
questions.why: KSR Part I Rule 76 proviso: none after one year from the date of sanction.

questions.q: Can an officer claim retrospective commutation of leave as a matter of right?
questions.why: KSR Part I Rule 89(i): the authority may commute, but it is not a right.

questions.q: Leave may be retrospectively commuted into a kind of leave admissible at what time?
options: On the date of the application for commutation
When the original leave was granted
On the date of joining duty

questions.q: What follows automatically when one kind of leave is commuted into another?
options: Drawal of arrears or recovery of amounts overdrawn

remember: Ordinary leave: earned, half-pay, commuted, leave not due and leave without allowances (Rule 77(i)).
Special leave: disability, maternity, paternity, child adoption and hospital leave (Rule 77(ii)).
Half-pay leave is earned for completed years of service (Rule 77(iv)).

questions.q: Which of these is included in 'ordinary leave'?
questions.why: KSR Part I Rule 77(i): earned, half-pay, commuted, leave not due and leave without allowances.

questions.q: Which of these is included in 'special leave'?
questions.why: KSR Part I Rule 77(ii) lists hospital leave among special leave.

questions.q: Half-pay leave is earned in respect of what?
An 'officer in permanent employ' is one who holds what?
options: Any post for over one year
A temporary post for five years
An officiating post for two years
A permanent post substantively, or a lien on one

remember: Half-pay leave: 20 days for each completed year of service (Rule 83), on private affairs or medical certificate (Rule 82).
Commuted leave: not more than half the half-pay leave due (Rule 84).
Twice the commuted leave is debited against half-pay leave (Rule 84).

questions.q: How many days of half-pay leave are admissible per completed year of service?
Half-pay leave may be availed on private affairs or on what other ground?
How much commuted leave can be granted?
options: Not more than half the half-pay leave due
Equal to the half-pay leave due
One-third of the half-pay leave due

questions.q: When commuted leave is granted, how much is debited against half-pay leave due?

remember: Rule 91: two years of continuous officiating or temporary service; covers the entire course, not broken periods.
Rule 91A: post-graduate course leave needs 5 years of continuous officiating or temporary service.
Rule 91 leave by authority competent for eligible leave and LWA; Rule 99 study leave only by Government.

questions.q: What minimum continuous service is needed for leave for superior qualifications under Rule 91?
questions.why: KSR Part I Rule 91: officiating or temporary service of two years or more.

questions.q: Is Rule 91 leave given for broken periods?
options: Yes, for any part of the course
Yes, but only for six months
No, it covers the entire period of the course
Yes, only in the final year

questions.q: What service is needed for post-graduate course leave under Rule 91A?
Who alone can sanction study leave under Rule 99?
questions.why: KSR Part I Rule 91 Government Decision: Rule 99 study leave only by Government.

remember: Full charge of a second post: special allowance not over 6 per cent of the minimum of that scale (Rule 53(b)(1)).
Current duties only: not over 3 per cent (Rule 53(b)(3)).
Allowed only if charge exceeds 14 working days (full) or one month (current duties); never beyond three months (Rule 53(c)).

questions.q: Special allowance for full additional charge must not exceed what share of the minimum of the other post's scale?
Special allowance for current duties only of an additional post must not exceed what?
options: 6 per cent of the minimum of the scale
3 per cent of the maximum of the scale
3 per cent of the minimum of the scale of that post
1 per cent of the minimum of the scale

questions.q: Special allowance for full additional charge is allowed only if the charge exceeds how long?
questions.why: KSR Part I Rule 53(c): 14 working days for full charge, one month for current duties only.

questions.q: What is the maximum period for which special allowance for additional charge can be allowed?
questions.why: KSR Part I Rule 53(c): not exceeding three months on any account.

remember: Casual leave: at most 20 days a calendar year; teaching staff 15 days (App VII para 2(i)).
Casual leave with holidays: resulting absence not over fifteen days at a stretch.
Casual leave is not recognised as leave, so it cannot be retrospectively commuted (para 7).

questions.q: What is the maximum casual leave in a calendar year for an officer?
questions.why: KSR Part I Appendix VII para 2(i).

questions.q: Teaching staff of educational institutions are eligible for how many days of casual leave in a year?
questions.why: KSR Part I Appendix VII para 2(i).

questions.q: Casual leave combined with holidays must not result in absence exceeding how long at a stretch?
questions.why: KSR Part I Appendix VII para 2(ii).

questions.q: Can casual leave be retrospectively commuted into another kind of leave?
options: No, as it is not recognised as leave
questions.why: KSR Part I Appendix VII para 7.

remember: Honorarium only with prior Government consent and amount settled in advance (Rule 49).
One-third of a non-recurring fee over Rs 2000 or recurring fee over Rs 1250 a year goes to General Revenues (Rule 48).
No outside work or fee without Government sanction (Rule 47).

questions.q: An honorarium should not be sanctioned unless the work had whose prior consent?
What share of a non-recurring fee exceeding Rs 2000 is credited to General Revenues?
A recurring fee exceeding what amount a year attracts credit of one-third to General Revenues?
An officer may undertake work for a private body or accept a fee only with whose sanction?
An honorarium's amount must be settled when?
options: At the end of the year
questions.why: KSR Part I Rule 49: the amount must be settled in advance.

remember: Leave with allowances is cancelled for the period of suspension; subsistence allowance is paid (Rule 55B(ii)).
On leave without allowances, no subsistence allowance during leave; payable on expiry if suspension continues (Rule 55B(i)).

questions.q: An officer on leave with allowances is suspended. What is the effect on the leave?
options: It is cancelled for the period of suspension
It is converted to half-pay leave
It is converted to leave without allowances

questions.q: An officer on leave with allowances is suspended. What is he entitled to?
An officer on leave without allowances is suspended. Is subsistence allowance payable during that leave?
options: Yes, from the date of suspension

questions.q: When does subsistence allowance become payable to an officer suspended during leave without allowances?
options: On expiry of the leave, if suspension continues

remember: Leave and extension are applied for in Form No. 13 to the competent authority (Rule 113).
Audit Officer keeps the leave account of gazetted officers; Head of Office keeps it for non-gazetted officers (Rule 112 Note).

questions.q: On which form is an application for leave made?
An application for leave must be made to whom?
options: The authority competent to grant the leave

questions.q: Who maintains the leave account of a gazetted officer?
Who maintains the leave account of a non-gazetted officer?
options: The Head of the Office in which he is employed

remember: Government may dispense with or relax a rule causing undue hardship in a particular case (Rule 7).
In doubt whether the rules apply to a person, refer to Government; its decision is final (Rule 4).

questions.q: Who may dispense with or relax a rule that causes undue hardship?
A rule may be relaxed when Government is satisfied of what?
options: That the officer has asked for it
That it causes undue hardship in a particular case
That the Head of Office agrees

questions.q: If doubt arises whether the rules apply to a person, to whom is it referred?
What is the nature of the Government's decision on such doubt?
options: It is open to appeal to the Audit Officer
It is valid for one year only
It needs approval of the Head of Office
questions.why: KSR Part I Rule 4: the decision of the Government shall be final.

remember: On substantive appointment to a permanent post, the officer acquires a lien on it and loses any earlier lien (Rule 16).
A lien cannot be terminated, even with consent, if it leaves him with no lien or suspended lien on a permanent post (Rule 19(a)).

questions.q: An officer is substantively appointed to a permanent post. What happens to his earlier lien on another post?
options: It is suspended for one year
It passes to the next senior officer

questions.q: On substantive appointment to a permanent post, the officer acquires what?
options: A right to pension at once

questions.q: Can a lien be terminated with the officer's consent if it leaves him with no lien on a permanent post?
options: Yes, with Head of Office approval

questions.q: A lien may in no circumstances be terminated if the result leaves the officer without what?
options: A lien or suspended lien on a permanent post

remember: Except for inefficiency or misbehaviour, or on his written request, no substantive transfer to a lower-paid post (Rule 21(a)).
Transfer means movement from one headquarter station to another (Rule 12(36)).

questions.q: Under Rule 21(a), an officer may be transferred to a post carrying less pay on account of what?
questions.why: KSR Part I Rule 21(a): inefficiency or misbehaviour, or his written request.

questions.q: An officer may be transferred to a lower-paid post on his own request in what form?
What does 'transfer' mean under Rule 12(36)?
options: Movement from one headquarter station to another

questions.q: Under Rule 21(a), an officer shall not be transferred substantively to a post carrying what?
options: More pay than his permanent post
Equal pay to his permanent post
Less pay than his permanent post

remember: On reinstatement after full exoneration, full pay and allowances as if never dismissed, removed, compulsorily retired or suspended (Rule 56(2)).
Payment is limited to three years immediately preceding reinstatement or superannuation (Rule 56(4) proviso).

questions.q: An officer is reinstated after being fully exonerated. What pay is he given?
options: Full pay and allowances as if not dismissed

questions.q: Payment on reinstatement is restricted to what period?
options: Three years immediately preceding reinstatement or superannuation

questions.q: Rule 56(2) pay applies as if the officer had not been dismissed, removed, compulsorily retired or what else?
How many years is the limit on payment under Rule 56(4)?

remember: Superannuation pension is granted to an officer entitled or compelled, by rule, to retire at a particular age (Part III Rule 55).

questions.q: To whom is a superannuation pension granted?
options: An officer entitled or compelled by rule to retire at a particular age
An officer who resigns at will

questions.q: Superannuation pension is linked to retirement at what?
options: A particular age fixed by rule
A fixed number of leave days
questions.why: KSR Part III Rule 55: retirement at a particular age.

questions.q: Under which KSR Part and Rule is superannuation pension defined?
questions.why: The quote is from KSR Part III, Rule 55.

remember: Invalid pension: for an employee certified by a Medical Board or Medical Officer as permanently incapacitated for public service (Part III Rule 42(2)).

questions.q: Who certifies an employee as permanently incapacitated for invalid pension?
options: A Medical Board or Medical Officer

questions.q: Invalid pension is granted for what kind of incapacity?
Which rule deals with invalid pension?
questions.why: The quote is KSR Part III Rule 42(2).

remember: Compassionate allowance to a dismissed or removed employee must not exceed two-thirds of the pension he would have got on retirement on that date (Part III Rule 5(a)).

questions.q: What is the limit on a compassionate allowance to a dismissed employee?
The limit is computed on the pension he would have got if he retired on what date?
options: The date of dismissal or removal

questions.q: To whom can such a compassionate allowance be granted?

remember: Pension application must be submitted at least one year before anticipated retirement, in Form 11 (Part III Rule 110).

questions.q: How early must a formal pension application be submitted?
options: At least one year before anticipated retirement

questions.q: Who must submit a formal application for pension?
The pension application is submitted in which form?
questions.why: KSR Part III Rule 110 (application in Form 11).

remember: An employee may not retire with a view to being re-employed and drawing pension in addition to pay (Part III Rule 91).

questions.q: Can an employee retire in order to be re-employed and draw pension plus pay?
options: Yes, with Head of Office approval

questions.q: An employee may not retire with the view to being re-employed and drawing what in addition to pay?
Which rule bars retiring in order to be re-employed with pension and pay?
